chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife, and he had touched everything from her, except that he did not copulate with her. Is there a waiting period for her? So he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was tested with this, so his father, Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), said to him: If he closed the door and lowered the curtain, the dower and the waiting period become obligatory.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dower and waiting period if a man divorces his wife after intimacy but before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the legal distinction between partial and full intimacy in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that seclusion (khalwah) with complete physical contact obligates the full dower (mahr) and the waiting period (iddah). It highlights the scholarly precedent set by Imam al-Baqir, who derived this ruling from his father, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn, emphasizing the importance of physical privacy as a condition for marital rights. This ruling underscores the principle that consummation is defined not solely by penetration but by the totality of intimate contact within a private setting.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man who divorces the woman and he had touched everything from her except that he did not copulate with her, is there a waiting period for her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the door is locked, and the curtain is pulled, it Obligates the dower and the waiting period’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces a woman whom he has touched without sexual intercourse if waiting period is obligatory. He (the Imam) said, ‘Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, had faced such a condition and his father, Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, said, ‘When doors are closed and curtains are pulled down mahr (dower) and waiting period become necessary.’”

Ibn abu ‘Umayr has said that Ahadith are not the same about this issue if mahr (dower) is complete or not. Certain ones have said that it is one-half of mahr (dower) and it means that a judge rules according to apparent condition of a case. When the doors are closed and curtains are pulled down mahr (dower) becomes obligatory. It is up to her when she knows before Allah that he has not touched then she deserves only half of mahr (dower).’”
